---
applyTo: "src/apps/pinch/**"
---

# Pinch rules

Applies on top of CLAUDE.md to everything under `src/apps/pinch/`. Keep the other copy of this file identical in body.

- **Theme: a chef's apron, clean first.** Surfaces are white on white by day and black on black by night, set apart by hairline borders and a soft shadow only where something floats (the nav pill, a popover, a sheet). Buttons are ink-filled (`--color-primary` is near-black, near-white in dark) for the one action on a screen and see-through with a hairline for the rest; never a block of orange. The warm orange is a drizzle, `--pinch-drizzle`, and appears only as a small touch: the today dot (`--pinch-drizzle-fill` with `--pinch-drizzle-fill-foreground`, the only place text sits on the orange), a selected outline, the selected day's ring, the active tab icon, the default product's star, the dashed "New" pills. The palette, radii, hairlines and field inset live in `pinch.css` as tokens on `html.pinch-theme`, switched on by `usePinchTheme()` while the app is mounted so portaled modals and drawers match. Change the look there, not per component, use semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `bg-secondary`) and the drizzle variable (`text-[var(--pinch-drizzle)]`) rather than raw colors, and body and row text stays the normal color (the tertiary-button rule in `pinch.css`). The app icon and banner follow the other apps: a black tile or banner, the white mark and name, and "Moondreams Dev" in grey.
- **Shape language.** Corners are set by the raised `--radius-*` tokens, so don't hand-roll radii. Options a person picks among are `Pill`s, never radios or a tab strip; an option is a hairline pill and the selected one gets a drizzle outline so its emoji stays readable. Navigation is a floating pill at the bottom of a phone, as wide as its three tabs and never stretched across the screen (Calendar, Recipes, Kitchen: `PinchNav`), and the same tabs stand in a rail on the left edge from `lg` up. Later Kitchen entries join the Kitchen tab and never add a fourth.
- **Wide screens use the width, not a stretched phone.** From `lg` the calendar fills the page with the meal's title in each cell (first item, `+N` for more) where a phone shows thin colour bars, and Recipes and Kitchen run in two columns; the phone layout is unchanged. Check a new screen at 1280px as well as 390px.
- **Emoji carry meaning.** Meals are 🍳 breakfast, 🥪 lunch, 🍝 dinner, 🍿 snack, 🍰 dessert, 🥤 drink, in that order; the same six colors are the `--pinch-meal-*` tokens, used on the calendar's thin bars. Ingredients get their vendored Twemoji icon, or the jar glyph when none fits; never a sparkle for "other".
- **Missing details appear only as in-context nudge lines.** A missing price, package size or nutrition value is one quiet line where it changes a number ("2 ingredients need a price · Add prices"), with a close button and a short fill-in sheet. Never a to-do list, a badge, a required field or a setup step, and a total always says what it leaves out ("$14.20 · leaves out 2 ingredients").
- **Three layers, recipes name only the ingredient.** Family, ingredient, product. A recipe or meal refers to an ingredient id, never a store or product; prices live on products. Copies that leave the app (Markdown) never carry prices, stores or products.
- **The nudge lives on the drawers, not in the plate builder.** The recipe, saved meal, day and planned meal views carry "Add prices" (closing the drawer before the fill-in sheet opens); the meal builder is a full-screen subview, so it states "Cost $0.08 · leaves out 4 ingredients" in text and nothing opens over it. A frozen day has no nudge, since a new price can't change it.
- **"Yours" is what you added, adjusted, priced or cook with.** Custom ingredients, adjusted catalog ones, ones with a product and ones a recipe uses; typing in the search looks through every ingredient, so a first-run kitchen never hears "nothing matches" for something the catalog has. Removing an in-use recipe, ingredient or store says it is taken off your lists, not erased, and a store the person adds back from the list comes back.
- **Vendored assets keep their licence.** The icons under `public/vendor/ingredient-icons` are Twemoji (CC-BY 4.0); the notice sits beside them and surfaces in Settings' About row once it exists. Add any new vendored set the same way.
- **Check lists at scale.** Pinch needs an oversized seed fixture like Waypoint's (`scripts/seeds/pinchScale.ts`, "Big Kitchen (scale test)"). Open new lists on it at phone width with the dev build throttled, and keep per-row work cheap (CLAUDE.md "Performance is a design check"): catalog groups mount only near the viewport (`LazyMount` plus `defer-offscreen`).
